subject: Temporary regional capacity & escalation matrix for SFO maintenance
messages:
From: Maria Torres <maria.torres@clearharbor.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: ops-oncall@clearharbor.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Planned SFO maintenance window — impact to SLA and on-call coverage?

Hi Ben,

Heads up — our SFO cloud provider has scheduled a region-wide maintenance window next week (Dec 4, 02:00–06:00 PST). Some of our networking tiers will be degraded for short intervals; our internal mitigation assumes up to 40% request amplification and periodic latency spikes.

Before we finalize our runbook, we need confirmation from Redwood on two things:

- Will Redwood be able to meet our P1/P2 response commitments during that window (we currently expect P1 within 30 minutes, P2 within 2 hours)?
- If not, can we agree a temporary exception (explicit coverage carve-in) including an escalation matrix so our ops team knows who to call?

I attached our vendor maintenance plan (SFO_maintenance_plan_v2.pdf).

We want to avoid a formal SLA credit request but need an operational plan that keeps our incident lifecycle short. Can you propose a short-term coverage / escalation playbook by EOD Monday?

Thanks,
Maria Torres
Head of Ops, ClearHarbor

---
Attachment: SFO_maintenance_plan_v2.pdf (PDF, 312KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Maria Torres <maria.torres@clearharbor.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Planned SFO maintenance window — impact to SLA and on-call coverage?

Maria — thanks for the heads up and for the plan. Short answer: we can support a temporary, documented carveout with tightened escalation routes so ClearHarbor still gets predictable response times. Proposed items below — happy to formalize into an amendment.

High-level proposal (operational only — not a permanent SLA change):
- Maintenance window covered: 2026-12-04 02:00–06:00 PST (matches your vendor notice).
- Temporary P1 target: 60 minutes from alerting during the window (we'll keep higher urgency triage).
- Temporary P2 target: 4 hours from alerting during the window.
- Coverage model: Redwood will activate a regional on-call carve-in. One designated responder on-call in SFO region + a secondary backup. We will not rely on global rotation during the 4-hour window.
- Escalation chain: responder -> Karthik Iyer (Senior Oncall Lead) -> Irene Choi (Support Engineering Manager) -> Ben Carter (Customer Success). Phone numbers and after-hours pager are in the attached CSV.
- Monitoring thresholds: we will set automated page thresholds to avoid noise; we'll share the minor/major delta thresholds before the window.
- SLAs & credits: this will be a documented temporary operational amendment (no automatic credits unless we miss the carved targets and you submit a credit request within 10 business days).

Next steps I propose:
1) I attach a draft "temp_escalation_matrix.csv" with named responders and phone/pager.
2) If you approve, we prepare a one-page amendment to the MSA and a DocuSign for signature (I can route to Legal).
3) We run a 30-minute pre-window coordination call (30 Nov 10:00 PST) to validate runbooks and thresholds.

If the temporary P1 60m / P2 4h is acceptable, reply-all and we'll lock it in and circulate the DocuSign.

Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0182

Thanks Ben — the proposal looks reasonable. A couple of clarifications before we sign: 

- Can you confirm whether Redwoods' regional responder will have permission to escalate to our incident bridge (we need the ability to add a Redwood responder as a participant in our bridge)?
- Please confirm the monitoring thresholds you'll use to trigger a P1 page (we want low false positives).
- We want the amendment to explicitly state this is temporary and limited to the maintenance window.

We can do the coordination call on Nov 30 at 10:00 PST — I'll send a calendar invite for the pre-window check. Once we review thresholds, we can sign the amendment on DocuSign.

Maria

Subject: Re: Planned SFO maintenance window — impact to SLA and on-call coverage?

Maria — great, thanks for the quick confirmation. Short note to capture agreed items and next steps so it's in-thread: 

Agreed operational items:
- Redwood to provide one regional responder + backup during the 2026-12-04 02:00–06:00 PST maintenance window.
- Temporary targets: P1 = 60 minutes, P2 = 4 hours (only active for the maintenance window).
- Redwood responder will be added to ClearHarbor's incident bridge when requested by ClearHarbor ops. We'll provide invite instructions ahead of the window.
- Monitoring thresholds: we'll use the following for pages during the window:
  * P1 page: sustained 3x baseline tail latency for >90s OR error rate spike >2% for 60s
  * P2 page: 1.5x baseline tail latency for >3m OR intermittent error rate >0.5% for 5m

Action items:
- Ben: route the amendment to Legal and create DocuSign by Tue 2026-12-01 EOD (Ben).
- Karthik: validate responder roster and confirm phone/pager numbers in temp_escalation_matrix.csv (Karthik).
- Irene: prepare runbook snippet for joining the ClearHarbor bridge and the post-incident notes template (Irene).
- Maria: confirm the calendar invite for the pre-window call on 2026-11-30 10:00 PST.

I'll mark this as an operational carveout limited to the specified window in our internal systems and update the console routing policy to force the regional responder for ClearHarbor during that period. If anything changes on your side, reply-all.

Thanks — talk tomorrow on the call.

Ben
